spring.title: Cherry blossom at Longwangtang
spring.note: Single-flowered varieties bloom around mid-April; double-flowered varieties follow roughly a week later.

spring.title: Cherry blossom at 203 Metre Hill
spring.note: The garden at the foot of 203 Metre Hill blooms about a week later than Longwangtang.

spring.title: Spring flowers on Dahei Shan
spring.note: Rhododendrons flower near the summit, with other spring flowers on the slopes. The ridge is often windy, so choose a calm day.

spring.title: Dalian Acacia Festival
spring.note: The black locust blossom festival has been held since 1990; in 2011 it ran from 25 to 31 May. Venues change from year to year.

spring.title: Blossom in the New Town
spring.note: Black locust trees line the streets of Taiyanggou in Lüshun.

spring.title: The forts before the leaves return
spring.note: Before the trees leaf out, the fortifications’ ditches and earthworks are easiest to see.

summer.title: Sweet cherries in Lüshun
summer.when: early June; from late May in warm years
summer.note: Since 2009, the district has held the title of China’s home of large sweet cherries. Trees grown outdoors flower in mid-April, and the fruit ripens 42 days later.

summer.title: Swimming season
summer.note: Some beaches remain closed in mid-July. In August 2026, water temperatures ranged from 24–30 °C in bulletins from China’s Ministry of Ecology and Environment.

summer.title: The sea below Golden Hill
summer.note: Lüshun’s town beach lies at the foot of the hill, beside Electric Cliff Battery.

summer.title: Shade at Fortification No. 5
summer.note: The fortification stands in woodland, cooler in hot weather than the exposed hills.

summer.title: Dalian’s port and waterfront
summer.note: Gangwan Square and the passenger terminal offer convenient views of the port.

autumn.title: The fishing season opens
autumn.note: The fishing ban in the Yellow and Bohai seas runs from 1 May until 12:00 on 1 September. Dalian marks its end with celebrations as boats leave the ports.

autumn.title: Ginkgo trees in Labour Park
autumn.note: The park is described as one of Dalian’s best places to see golden ginkgo leaves.

autumn.title: The land front on a clear day
autumn.note: The weather is dry, the leaves are falling, and the heights offer views along the whole line of hills.

autumn.title: The view from Quail Hill
autumn.note: In autumn, views across the harbour and hills reach farther than in the humid summer.

winter.title: The Russian cemetery in winter
winter.note: Visitors bring flowers on anniversaries of the defence; there are few people.

winter.title: 5 December: the loss of 203 Metre Hill
winter.note: On this day in 1904, Russian troops abandoned 203 Metre Hill, giving the enemy a view into the harbour.

winter.title: 15 December: Kondratenko’s death
winter.note: A stone at Fort No. II marks the place where the general was killed.

winter.title: 2 January: the fortress surrenders
winter.note: The surrender was signed on 20 December 1904 (2 January 1905). Stessel met Nogi at Shuishiying on 23 December (5 January).

winter.title: 9 February: the war begins
winter.note: Japanese destroyers attacked the squadron off Port Arthur at night. Quail Hill offers the best view of the harbour.
